best_for: Nextcloud or ownCloud users who want their notes as plain Markdown files on disk, with old versions, sharing and to-do lists handled by their own server.

points.title: Your notes stay plain files
points.text: Each note is a Markdown text file in a folder you choose. Any editor or sync tool can open it, so leaving QOwnNotes later means nothing to export.

points.title: Built around your own server
points.text: A sync tool such as the Nextcloud client moves the files. With your Nextcloud or ownCloud server connected, the app can restore older versions and trashed notes, share notes, and manage to-dos through Nextcloud Tasks or another CalDAV server.

points.title: Encryption and scripts
points.text: Single notes can be locked with built-in AES-256 encryption, or with PGP or Keybase through example scripts. A script repository inside the app adds features with a click.

points.title: Phones get companions, not a twin
points.text: The desktop app is the main product. Android has a separate QOwnNotes app on F-Droid that works with local note folders, a Nextcloud app shows notes in the browser, and a web app sends photos from your phone into the open desktop note.

points.title: Free under the GPL
points.text: QOwnNotes is free and open source under GPL-2.0, made by Patrizio Bekerle, with an optional donation.

points.title: Mac: expect a Gatekeeper warning
points.text: The macOS download is a universal disk image for macOS 13 or later. On first launch macOS says the developer cannot be verified, and you open it through right-click or Security settings. The Homebrew cask is disabled because it fails Apple's Gatekeeper check, and the Mac listing here is at 26.9.0 while Windows has 26.11.6.

points.title: Versions kept
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 230 versions, as an MSI installer or a zip. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need the GitHub releases page. The Linux Flatpak, for x64 and Arm64, is marked verified by Flathub as published by the developer.
